one_liner: Pumble has a self-serve REST API (free-plan API-keys addon plus OAuth2 apps via the Pumble SDK) and an official hosted MCP server, so a toolkit is buildable now.
auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization-code flow for Pumble apps (clientId/clientSecret, access token, plus an x-app-token header). A simpler API key is generated via the API Keys addon and sent as a bearer token or header.
access_notes: The API addon is available on all plans, including Free. The Free plan allows three apps/integrations. Creating an app from scratch in Configure apps gives credentials.
blocker_notes: The API Keys addon must be installed by a workspace user. Rate limits are modest (about 100 requests/user/minute in the OAuth API docs, 1000/min for API keys).

evidence.quote: Pumble uses OAuth2 in order to allow your app to access the API.
you must first generate an API key within your Pumble workspace administration panel. This token must be passed inside the HTTP header of every request as a bearer token.
It is **available on all** [**Pumble plans**](https://pumble.com/pricing)** to Owners, Admins, and Members**.
A Pumble workspace where you are allowed to install apps. The free Pumble plan is enough.
Default limitation is 100 requests per user per minute (per token header) and 500 per app (per x-app-token header).
This addon lets you generate an API key that allows you to send messages, reactions, and more via simple HTTP requests.
Pumble maintains a native MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosted directly at pumble.com
With the Pumble Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, you can connect third-party AI agents (e.g., Claude, Gemini, Codex) to Pumble
